overall: The AG found Chair Benson did not violate the Open Meeting Law: his December 8 and December 15 summary emails memorialized open-meeting discussions and were not deliberation outside a posted meeting. No remedy was ordered.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Chair deliberated by email outside a posted meeting via his December 8 'BOS-Updates' summary of the December 7 meeting, which they said was opinionated.
allegations.key_passage: Although the email was sent to a quorum of the Board and could be construed to include the Chair’s opinion on a matter within the Board’s jurisdiction, we find that, on the whole, the email simply memorialized the discussions that occurred during the meeting, and therefore the circulation of the email merely served an administrative purpose similar to circulating draft minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Chair deliberated by email outside a posted meeting via his December 15 'BOS-Updates' summary of the December 14 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Thus, we find that the December 15 email did not constitute deliberation outside of a properly posted meeting and therefore did not violate the Open Meeting Law.
